answer: To join, an applicant must close a chain of 10,000 puzzles keyed to its own public key. Each solved step feeds the next like a river: one vertex unlocks the next, and no step can start before the one before it finishes, so a hundred cores finish one identity no faster than one. When the chain closes, the registry stamps a violet seal naming that key alone. One chain costs 83 hours of single-core work, about $12 in rented compute; 5,000 fake identities would burn $60,000 and 415,000 core-hours, and a chain solved for one key shortens no other chain by a second.
